extracted.intended_audience: students, teachers, and enthusiasts of olympiad geometry (AoPS community / math olympiad training)
extracted.subtask_description: An index/collection page that gathers geometry problems (and sometimes solutions/PDFs) from international, national, regional, and training olympiads, organized by contest, year, and round, often with AoPS links. Useful as a resource for preparation, study, and reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection scope and content
rubrics_metrics.description: "Geometry Problems from IMOs olympiad geometry problems with aops links geometry articles, books, magazines, shortlists for Juniors and Seniors problem collections with solutions from National, Regional and International Mathematical Olympiads latest added on the right menu" (page lists contests, years, rounds, and problem statements/PDFs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries are organized by contest (international, regional, national, TSTs, juniors), year, and round; items often include AoPS links and/or PDFs; missing years/problems are explicitly noted. Use this structure when contributing or using the collection: label items by contest/year/round, indicate missing entries, and link to AoPS/PDFs where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of AoPS links in item names
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit note on the page: "with aops links in the names" (e.g., problem entries indicate AoPS links in their labels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When listing problems, include AoPS links in the problem titles/names to provide direct access to discussions/solutions; annotate if a problem is missing from AoPS. This is a practical presentation standard used across the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A few notations, line related: "(AB) is an open segment  [AB] a closed segment  \overline{AB} an orientated segment  (AB a ray  [AB a closed ray  AB a line" (as listed on the page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page defines and uses specific notational conventions for segments, rays, oriented segments, and lines; follow these conventions when reading or adding problem statements to maintain consistency with the collection.
